plan.summary: A standard 12-month run on MSFT (NASDAQ), USD, as of 2026-09-25, built around three operator questions: is cloud margin expansion durable or flattered by capitalisation; what must be true for the current multiple; how much growth is AI revenue absent three years ago. Evidence is primary: the FY2026 10-K (segment, revenue, PP&E, lease, commitments, SBC notes) with FY2023-FY2025 comparatives, FY2026 10-Qs, 8-K earnings exhibits, XBRL facts, and dated market and rate data. This revision adds the forward fixed-charge pipeline (leases signed but not yet commenced; purchase and construction obligations by period), share-based compensation, a defined multiple with its denominator filing line, a dated forward-expectations benchmark, and named provenance for every non-filing valuation input, with the reverse-DCF reported as a solved range. Sources are priority-ranked; P3 items are droppable and the report states what was not reached. No figure is stated here and no fact asserted. Prior research supplied with the request is not-evidence: it shapes questions only and is never cited.

challenges.statement: The durability question turns on fixed charges not yet in the income statement, but the plan names only assets under construction and current lease classification. It does not ask for the lease note's disclosure of leases signed but not yet commenced, nor the purchase and construction commitments table, which are where the forward depreciation and rent pipeline is disclosed. Without them, 'how much of the fixed charge has not yet begun to run' is answered from PP&E alone and understates the committed step-up.
challenges.suggestion: Add to earnings_quality and cash_flow_analysis an explicit retrieval of the lease note's not-yet-commenced lease commitments and the commitments note's purchase/construction obligations by period, across FY2024-FY2026, and state the question as: what committed fixed charge exists that no period yet reflects?

challenges.statement: The reverse-DCF is the whole answer to operator question two, yet the only discount-rate input with a named source is the Treasury curve. Equity risk premium, beta or cost-of-equity method, cost of debt, forecast horizon length and terminal-growth convention are unsourced. A recorded calculation cannot be auditable if its most outcome-sensitive inputs enter without provenance; the risk register calls the output sensitive to these but does not fix where they come from.
challenges.suggestion: Name a dated, citable source or a stated platform convention for each non-filing valuation input (ERP, beta or cost-of-equity method, cost of debt, horizon, terminal growth), and require the reverse-DCF to be reported as a solved range across those inputs rather than a single implied path.

challenges.statement: 'The current multiple' is never defined and no source establishes the expectations embedded in it. Market data supplies price and share count only; there is no planned source for the earnings or cash-flow denominator convention, nor for prevailing forward expectations. The plan tests the implied path only against disclosed history, which can show whether the path is unprecedented but not whether it differs from what the market is currently being told to expect.
challenges.suggestion: State in valuation_dcf which multiple is being decomposed and its denominator's filing line, and add a dated source for current market expectations (consensus or company guidance from the FY2026 Q4 earnings release) so the implied path can be compared with a forward benchmark as well as with history.

challenges.statement: The AI-revenue fallback rests on management assertions in earnings releases and prepared remarks, but no risk names that such metrics are management-defined and frequently non-comparable across periods: run-rate versus recognised revenue, bookings or contracted commitments versus revenue, and definitions that are restated or retired between quarters. Labelling them 'assertion' does not prevent a growth series being built from quantities that do not mean the same thing in each period.
challenges.suggestion: Require growth_outlook to record, for every management AI figure, the exact wording, the period, the stated definition and any change in definition versus the prior quarter, and to refuse to chain figures across quarters whose definitions differ.

challenges.statement: Share-based compensation appears in no section focus and no source description. It bears directly on both operator questions the plan takes most seriously: it is a non-cash charge sitting between operating income and operating cash flow in the very gap cash_flow_analysis is asked to construct, and its treatment determines the steady-state margin the reverse-DCF solves for. As drafted, earnings quality is scoped to capitalisation and depreciation only.
challenges.suggestion: Add SBC to earnings_quality (charge by year and as a share of revenue, from the cash flow statement and equity note) and state explicitly in valuation_dcf whether SBC is treated as an expense or added back, since the implied margin is not interpretable without that convention.

challenges.statement: Fifteen source entries spanning four 10-Ks, three 10-Qs, two fiscal years of 8-K exhibits, transcripts, two peer 10-Ks, XBRL frames, full-text search and two regulators is a large retrieval load for a standard-mode run. Nothing in the plan orders the work, so a budget or availability failure could land on the PP&E, lease and commitments notes that carry the operator's central question rather than on the peripheral comparisons.
challenges.suggestion: Rank the sources: FY2026 10-K notes (PP&E, lease, segment, revenue, commitments and contingencies) first, then the FY2023/FY2025 comparatives, with peer filings, proxy and regulator documents marked as droppable, and state what the report says if a lower-ranked source is not reached.

critique.coverage_note: Critiqued the summary, twelve section focuses, fifteen sources and ten named risks. The plan's disclosure-limit risks (no AI line, non-GAAP cloud aggregate, no segment depreciation) are honestly stated and I did not re-raise them. Challenges concentrate on committed-but-unrecognised fixed charges, unsourced valuation inputs, an undefined multiple, SBC, definitional drift in management AI metrics, and retrieval prioritisation.

sections.focus: Direct answers to the three operator questions, each tagged as measured from filed evidence or as judgement, with unresolved items named. Carries only stored facts and recorded calculations from later sections. Closes with an explicit list of planned sources not retrieved and the claims left unsized as a result.

Core of the margin-durability question. From the PP&E and accounting-policy notes: stated useful lives for server and network equipment, any change in estimate and the filing's quantification of its period effect; capitalised software and capitalised interest; capitalisation of SBC into software or PP&E. Compare gross PP&E and assets under construction against the depreciation charge. Add share-based compensation by year and as a share of revenue, from the cash flow statement and the SBC/equity note, FY2023-FY2026. Name what is not disclosed, notably depreciation by segment.

Operating cash flow, additions to PP&E, finance lease principal payments and cash paid for lease liabilities, FY2023-FY2026, plus the SBC add-back so the gap between operating income and cash generation is decomposed rather than asserted. Then the committed-but-unrecognised pipeline: the lease note's leases signed but not yet commenced with amounts and expected commencement dates, and the commitments note's purchase and construction obligations by period, FY2024-FY2026. The question stated as: what committed fixed charge exists that no reported period yet reflects?

Reported segment revenue and operating income for Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud and More Personal Computing across FY2023-FY2026 and the FY2026 quarters, from the segment note. Separate the auditable segment margin path from the non-GAAP 'Microsoft Cloud' aggregate used in earnings releases, which spans segments and is not an audited reporting unit. Flag any recast or cost reallocation that breaks comparability, quoting the filing's own description.

How much growth is AI revenue that did not exist three years ago. Establish first whether the filings disclose any AI revenue category; if not, fall back on revenue by product and service category FY2023-FY2026, remaining performance obligations and deferred revenue. For every management AI figure, record verbatim wording, the period, the stated definition (run-rate, bookings, contracted commitment or recognised revenue) and any change or retirement of that definition versus the prior quarter. Figures whose definitions differ are not chained into a series; the break is reported.

Four-year income statement, margin and returns history from the FY2026 and FY2023 10-K comparatives, giving the base against which the recent cloud and AI period is judged: revenue growth, gross and operating margin, R&D and sales and marketing intensity, SBC intensity and effective tax rate, each sourced to a specific filing and statement line.

State which multiple is decomposed and its denominator's filing line (EV to FY2026 operating income and EV to operating cash flow less additions to PP&E, both from named statement lines). Enterprise value from price and share count on 2026-09-25 plus debt, lease liabilities, cash and investments from the balance sheet. SBC is treated as an expense, never added back; any variant is reported separately and labelled. Every non-filing input carries provenance: risk-free rate from the dated Treasury curve, ERP from a dated published series, beta with stated estimation window, cost of debt from the debt note coupons plus a dated corporate yield index, ten-year explicit horizon, terminal growth bounded by the as-of-date 10y yield.

The reverse-DCF answering what would have to be true for the current multiple. Solve for the revenue growth path, steady-state operating margin and terminal growth implied by price, reported as a range across the named ERP, beta, cost-of-debt and terminal-growth grid rather than a single implied path. Test the implied path against disclosed history and against a dated forward benchmark (consensus estimates, or company guidance from the Q4 FY2026 earnings release if consensus is unavailable). Sensitivities isolate the depreciation and rent step-up from the committed pipeline and the pace of AI revenue scaling.

State the thesis as a small number of falsifiable conditions tied to disclosed line items: utilisation-driven margin holding as committed depreciation and rent enter the income statement; AI-attributable revenue growing faster than the fixed-cost base; SBC intensity not absorbing the margin gain. Each condition paired with the filing line and the future disclosure that would confirm or break it inside the 12-month horizon.

Risks sized from filings where possible and explicitly marked unsized where not: committed fixed charges against uncontracted demand, using the commitments and not-yet-commenced lease disclosures; customer, partner and counterparty concentration the revenue note may not disaggregate; goodwill and intangible carrying values; antitrust and cloud-licensing remedies; AI liability and emerging AI regulation. Source the commitments, contingencies and legal proceedings notes of the FY2026 10-K, which prior work indicates may not have been reviewed.

Dated events inside the 12-month horizon: scheduled FY2027 quarterly earnings releases and 10-Q filings, the FY2027 10-K, the annual meeting and proxy record date, and any regulatory decision or remedy deadline whose date appears in a primary regulator document. Each carries its source and the disclosure it would newly make available; undated expectations are labelled as such, including where a prior view named a meeting with no readable calendar date.

output.rationale: SIC 7372 matches Early-stage and loss-making technology, which blocks no valuation model: the standard model runs and no confirmation is needed.

peers.name: Apple Inc.
peers.rationale: Diversified large-cap tech with platform ecosystem, devices and services mix; less software-pure than MSFT but similar scale, margins scrutiny and investor overlap in mega-cap tech multiples.

peers.name: Alphabet Inc.
peers.rationale: Competes directly in cloud (GCP vs Azure), enterprise software/AI, and productivity tools; comparable scale and R&D intensity though ad revenue mix differs materially.

peers.name: AMAZON COM INC
peers.rationale: AWS is the primary hyperscale cloud competitor to Azure; overlap in cloud infrastructure economics though retail segment makes overall business mix less comparable.

peers.name: ORACLE CORP
peers.rationale: Enterprise software and database vendor increasingly competing in cloud infrastructure and applications; smaller scale but similar enterprise software economics and subscription transition.

peers.name: Salesforce, Inc.
peers.rationale: Pure-play enterprise SaaS competitor overlapping with Microsoft's Dynamics and productivity cloud offerings; smaller scale, useful for software subscription multiple comparison.

peers.name: ADOBE INC.
peers.rationale: Prepackaged software vendor with high-margin subscription model similar to Microsoft's productivity software segment, though narrower end-market focus on creative/marketing.

peers.name: INTERNATIONAL BUSINESS MACHINES CORP
peers.rationale: Enterprise software, cloud and hybrid infrastructure competitor with long enterprise relationships similar to Microsoft's enterprise base, though hardware/consulting mix dilutes comparability.

peers.name: SAP SE
peers.rationale: Global enterprise applications leader comparable to Microsoft's business software segment; foreign private issuer but ADR-listed and widely used for enterprise software multiple comparisons.

themes.label: AI infrastructure capital expenditure buildout
themes.rationale: MSFT is among the largest hyperscaler capex spenders, building out GPU-dense datacenters for Azure and OpenAI workloads; capex guidance and depreciation drag are directly tied to this cycle.

themes.label: Enterprise cloud migration and infrastructure spend
themes.rationale: Azure is a core growth engine reliant on continued enterprise migration off on-prem systems; Azure growth rate is a primary metric investors track for MSFT's cloud segment health.

themes.label: Generative AI product monetization
themes.rationale: Copilot embedding across Office, GitHub and Azure represents MSFT's attempt to monetize generative AI via seat-based and consumption pricing, directly affecting future revenue mix.

themes.label: Grid electrification and power constraints
themes.rationale: MSFT's datacenter expansion is increasingly gated by power availability and grid interconnection, pushing it into nuclear and renewable PPAs, tying capex timing to electrification bottlenecks.

refused_concepts.label: Share-based Compensation Arrangement by Share-based Payment Award, Fair Value Assumptions, Risk Free Interest Rate, Maximum

findings.statement: Beginning FY27, Microsoft is replacing its three reporting segments (Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, More Personal Computing) with two: 'Agents and Infra' (Azure, Microsoft 365 cloud, productivity/server licensing, industry solutions, frontier/support services) and 'Devices and Consumer' (search/advertising, XBOX, Windows OEM and devices).

CEO Satya Nadella frames the restructuring explicitly as a response to AI 'blurring the boundaries between our products and reshaping our business models,' i.e. the company itself states that its historical segment/product lines no longer map cleanly to how it operates or allocates resources.

Restated FY26 figures under the new structure show Agents and Infra full-year revenue of $268,127M and operating income of $155,237M (implied for combined FY26 restated total from the presentation), versus Devices and Consumer FY26 revenue of $63,712M and operating income of $18,872M — confirming Agents and Infra (cloud/AI/productivity) is overwhelmingly the larger and more profitable part of the business, not just the ad/consumer side commonly associated with 'Microsoft is a PC/Windows company.'

Under the new reporting, Azure is redefined to be 'more purely' a consumption-based infrastructure metric: GitHub cloud, other developer cloud services, and Security Copilot revenue move out of Azure and into the Microsoft 365 commercial cloud metric, and Healthcare and Life Sciences cloud moves out of Azure into the new Industry solutions cloud metric — meaning reported Azure growth rates before and after FY27 are not directly comparable on a like-for-like basis without restatement.

The FY27 restructuring also folds LinkedIn Marketing Solutions and LinkedIn Premium Subscriptions into the 'Search and advertising' metric (Devices and Consumer segment), and moves LinkedIn Talent/Sales Solutions plus Dynamics 365 into a new 'Industry solutions' metric (Agents and Infra segment) — splitting what was formerly reported as one 'LinkedIn' revenue line across two different segments.

Restated 'As Restated' product-and-service revenue table for FY26 full year shows Azure at $101,938M and Microsoft 365 cloud at $100,299M, versus the prior 'As Reported' basis showing Server products and cloud services at $129,425M and Microsoft 365 commercial products and cloud services at $101,997M — illustrating materially different segment-line revenue depending on reporting vintage, a point analysts should not conflate.

Microsoft explicitly states the new segment/product definitions 'will be used in our SEC filings going forward,' indicating this is a formal, durable change to disclosure structure rather than a one-off investor-relations reframing.

The FY27 investor metrics presentation (dated September 2026, filed as an 8-K exhibit) explicitly carries a forward-looking-statements disclaimer tying actual results to risk factors disclosed in the company's Form 10-K and 10-Q filings, underscoring that the segment change itself does not supersede or eliminate previously disclosed risk factors.

assumptions.name: exit_multiple
assumptions.justification: Cross-check, not a comp: EBITDA margin implied by the derived 44.2% EBIT plus 8.7% D&A is ~53%; at a 17.5% tax rate and capex settling near D&A, terminal FCF is ~0.65 of EBITDA, so 1/(0.09−0.03)≈16.7x FCF ≈ 11x EBITDA; if capex stays near the 20.3% mean it falls toward 8x. 13.0x leans to partial normalisation. Of the two, I regard the perpetual-growth figure as the better terminal estimate — this multiple hinges entirely on where capex settles, which no filing yet answers. Raise toward 18x only if capex reverts fully.

assumptions.name: revenue_growth
assumptions.justification: The compound annual growth rate of revenue from 2022-06-30 to 2026-06-30, over 4 year(s): revenue moved from 198,270,000,000 to 331,839,000,000. Held flat across the forecast, because a trailing rate is one number and projecting a fade is a judgement this derivation does not make.

assumptions.name: risk_free_rate
assumptions.justification: The US 10-year Treasury constant maturity yield was 5.11% on 2026-09-23, as published by 2026-09-25 (Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System (H.15), series DGS10). Taken as the USD risk-free rate for this run's as-of date and converted to the fraction 0.0511.

assumptions.name: tax_rate
assumptions.justification: The mean of income tax expense over pre tax income across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. The individual observations were 0.1311, 0.1898, 0.1823, 0.1763, 0.1940.

assumptions.name: terminal_growth
assumptions.justification: Taken as below a WACC of roughly 8.5–9.5% (5.11% 10y risk-free plus an ordinary large-cap equity premium); even a floor-case 7% WACC leaves ample spread. 3.0% is near long-run US nominal GDP, and the 5.11% risk-free implies a higher nominal-inflation regime than a 2.0–2.5% assumption would suit. I do not extend the derived 13.7% trailing growth into perpetuity: no firm outgrows the economy for ever. Lower to ~2.0–2.5% if you judge the Devices/Consumer drag or AI-capex competition caps real growth; the 4.0% cap is not warranted.

assumptions.name: working_capital_intensity
assumptions.justification: The mean of net working capital — current assets less current liabilities — over revenue, across 5 period(s) ending 2022-06-30, 2023-06-30, 2024-06-30, 2025-06-30, 2026-06-30. A negative figure is normal for a business paid before it pays, and is proposed as it stands rather than floored at zero.

The bridge from enterprise value to equity value is net debt alone. Associate holdings, minority interests and pension deficits are not read off the filings by this build, so a business carrying material non-operating items is valued as though it does not.
